nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges if and only if there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$.
nodes.title: Characterization of subhypergraph containment

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges when there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ edges of $H$ are subsets of $S$.
nodes.title: Subhypergraph containment

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting if and only if for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Characterization of intersecting families

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting when every two distinct members meet: for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Intersecting families

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform if and only if every member $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: Characterization of uniform hypergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform when every edge $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: Uniform hypergraphs

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
